This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode). REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT OVER FOOTPATHS, STREET AND PAVEMENTS: As per order no.68 dated 21.06.2024, Mr. Debashis Nayak, learned counsel appearing for the C.M.C. took time to submit a fresh report with video recording and photographs relating to the status of two areas i.e. (i) O.M.P. Square to Nuabazar and (ii) Link Road to Badambadi to show that the said two stretches are free from encroachments and debris have also been removed in the post clearance drive. Learned counsel for the C.M.C. placed some video footage of those aforesaid areas. The same was played in open Court today. But we found that in some areas, debris still have not been removed and there is some encroachment also. Learned counsel has assured this Court that he would discuss with the officials of the C.M.C. and ensure that they take immediate steps for removal of the encroachment, so also the debris. Put up this matter on 25.07.2024. (S.K. Sahoo) Judge (V. Narasingh) Judge 73 RE-ENCROACHMENT IN ENCROACHMENT FREE 27.06.2024 AREAS.
texts.facts: On 21.06.2024, Mr. G. Mathi Vathanan, Principal Secretary to Government, Department of Housing and Urban Development appeared through virtual mode and after having interaction with him, he assured this Court that he would pass necessary instruction to see that different problems, which are arising on account of water logging may be on account of not taking steps in terms of the contingency plan. It is reported that waste water of five drains are being discharged into the canal in gross violation of direction of this Court, Odisha Human Rights Commission and State Pollution Control Board.
texts.arguments: Mr. Dash, learned President of the High Court Bar Association has brought to our notice different news clippings of the local daily newspapers relating to water logging situation of various places of Cuttack City, which arose on account of rain on 25.06.2024. The learned President of the Orissa High Court Bar Association has also filed a memo relating to the temporary measures required to be undertaken for the monsoon season and it is mentioned therein that three 60 HP power pumps are required to be installed near junction points between BSWC and box drain at Kesarpur for discharge of drain water from the above noted BSWC to box drain. It is stated at the Bar that such pumps were earlier functioning at the said location and because of which water logging was minimized. Learned counsel for the C.M.C. drew the attention of this Court to order no.50 dated 16.05.2024, wherein he had made a submission that in different areas of Cuttack Town, parking areas have been specified but the space in those areas are not adequate and C.M.C. has to identify other available spaces exclusively for parking purpose.
